reasons: Claimed status is compliant and no redline or comment was proposed — the rendered text is identical to the original, which is the expected output for a compliant finding.

The cited text supports the classification: p0090 contains an express Vendor-to-Customer indemnity ('Garman agrees to indemnify Sparkling and hold it harmless') backed by an ownership/non-interference warranty, with the standard IP remedy ladder (procure right, procure equivalent, replace/modify) at p0091–p0093, i.e. the rule's fallback position.

Direction is correct — the indemnity runs from Vendor to us and no reverse or one-way Customer indemnity for Vendor's software/services is cited, so walk-away territory does not arise; p0105 further carves Sections 13/14 out of the liability cap and consequential-damages exclusion, which is better than the fallback's 3x super-cap and benefits us.

The failed deterministic check ('vendor indemnity for IP infringement present') is a phrasing artefact — the indemnity is framed as breach of the ownership/non-infringement warranty rather than using the words 'infringement claim' in the indemnity trigger — and the paragraph expressly addresses the infringement scenario, so the heuristic does not overturn the substance.

Shortfalls from the preferred position (no express 'defend'/control-of-defence and cooperation mechanic, no refund fallback remedy, no breach-of-law / data-breach / gross-negligence limbs, affiliates not named, tight ten-day notice condition) are correctly recorded in the rationale as sub-elements rather than escalated to a deviation, consistent with the playbook's classification semantics.
